citations.F1: `serialize_event` does one `actor` SELECT per event (N+1, ~1900 round trips for acme) — batch it into a single `WHERE id = ANY($actor_ids)` query and build a lookup dict.
citations.F2: Dedup bug: `if ev["dedupe_key"] in seen` against a growing `list` is O(n²) on top of everything else — use a `set`.
citations.F3: `lookup_geo` uses synchronous `requests.get` inside an async handler... blocks that worker's whole event loop for seconds at a time... fix by using an async HTTP client (httpx.AsyncClient) or moving geo lookups off the request path.
citations.F4: no index covers `(org_id, created_at)` — `events` only has indexes on `actor_id` and `kind`, so this is a sequential-scan-and-sort over 4.2M rows every call; add `CREATE INDEX events_org_created_idx ON events (org_id, created_at DESC)`
citations.F6: bound `_geo_cache` (LRU with a maxsize, or TTL)
citations.F9: Do not ship the on-call proposal as-is: it scales up two subsystems (workers, pool) and slaps a cache in front of a request that has three separate correctness/perf bugs — it will hide the symptom for ~60s windows and make the memory leak worse (more workers each running the same unbounded caches).
